draft.title: Context of reception
card: Context of reception is the time and place in which a text is read. It is about the readers, not the writer.
Readers bring their own values, beliefs and experiences to a text. These shape what they notice and what they think it means.
Values change over time and differ between places. So the same text can be read in different ways by readers in 1900 and readers today.
This is why interpretations of a text shift. A new reading does not have to cancel an older one, but it can bring out different ideas in the text.
draft.remember: Readers bring their own values, so the same text can be read differently as time and place change.

a.q: Why can a novel from 1900 be read differently by students today?
opts: Today's readers bring different values to it
The words in the novel have changed over time
The writer's circumstances have changed since 1900
Older novels have no fixed meaning at all
a.why: Readers bring their own values, and these differ from those of readers in 1900. The text itself has not changed. The writer's circumstances belong to a different idea, and the card does not say that meaning is absent.
a.clue: Think about who has changed, not the book.

b.q: A play is staged in 1950 and again today. Critics in 1950 praise a character's obedience as a virtue. Many critics today see it as a weakness. What best explains the difference?
opts: The two groups of readers hold different values
The playwright rewrote the play between the two stagings
The critics in 1950 misunderstood the play
The play was written in a different year each time
b.why: The critics read the same play but hold different values, so they judge the character differently. Nothing in the card says that one group must have misread it. The playwright's circumstances are not what has changed here.
b.clue: Look at what the two groups of critics bring to the play.

a.best: Today's readers bring different values to it

b.best: The two groups of readers hold different values
